acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc:
Hannah Jacoby tells the story of when she and her best friend Lindsey bonded over those toy soldiers with the parachutes, called (really) Poopatroopers — and how the little jumpers perfectly bookended their high-school years. And guest host Sarah Koenig explains the very interesting trends we discovered in our listeners' coincidences.
Sarah is the host of Serial. Her new podcast from The New York Times, METRO, is out this week.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc:
A surprising number of coincidences involve grandmothers. One grandma has so many coincidences happen to her that it drives her granddaughter, 16-year-old Juliana Bontrager, to try to beat her at her own coincidence game. We also hear from Blake Oliver about a very strange appearance his grandma once made.
You can hear more from Blake Oliver in an interview on The Story.
acts.title: Grandmas

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: When it comes to love, coincidences tend to loom extra-large. Stephen Lee tells about the time his parents first met his fiance’s parents, and his future mother-in-law dropped a coincidence bomb. And we hear how a dollar bill ended up clinching a marriage, after floating around Chicago for years.
acts.title: In God We Trust

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Ryan Rozar told us about a confounding coincidence that was visited on him in college. We didn’t think it was a coincidence at all, so we set out to prove him wrong.
acts.title: Brother, Can You Spare a Dime

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: More stories of dazzling coincidences: an old boyfriend is conjured in Morocco, a jazz singer seems to rise from the dead, and three boys believe they’ve seen a corpse. Plus stories of errant fathers, lost and found.
acts.title: Don't Lift the Manhole Cover

acts.label: Act Five
acts.desc:
Kerry Weeks tells about the time he lost a pocketknife and turned to the galaxy for help.
This story was recorded live at a Moth StorySLAM in New York City.
acts.title: What Are The Chances?
